root.label: References and temporaries
root.note: Reference initialization governs what expressions bind, when temporaries materialize, and how long they survive.

children.label: Reference binding rules
children.note: Four reference signatures accept distinct combinations of lvalues, rvalues, and constness.

children.label: Non-const lvalue T&
children.note: Binds exclusively to non-const lvalues and rejects temporaries or const objects.

children.label: Rvalue reference T&&
children.note: Binds exclusively to non-const xvalues and prvalues to enable resource stealing.

children.label: Universal const T&
children.note: Binds to lvalues, rvalues, and implicitly convertible expressions of different types.

children.label: Implicit conversion temporaries
children.note: Binding const T& across incompatible types materializes a fresh unrelated temporary object.

children.label: Type mismatch copy
children.note: Binding const int& to a double creates a separate int temporary unaffected by later writes.

children.label: C++23 detection traits
children.note: reference_constructs_from_temporary and reference_converts_from_temporary catch dangling binds.

children.label: Direct lifetime extension
children.note: Binding a local reference directly to a temporary extends its lifetime to that scope.

children.label: Full-expression baseline
children.note: Unextended temporaries destruct at the end of the enclosing full-expression in reverse order.

children.label: Subobject and aggregate
children.note: Binding a temporary's data member or aggregate reference field extends the whole temporary.

children.label: Where extension stops
children.note: Syntactic indirection through calls or constructors cancels temporary lifetime extension.

children.label: Function call return
children.note: Passing a temporary through an identity function or accessor lets it die at the semicolon.

children.label: Constructor member init
children.note: Binding a temporary to a reference member inside a constructor always dangles after construction.

children.label: Return and new expressions
children.note: Temporaries bound inside return statements or new expressions never extend past their context.

children.label: Range-for and P2718R0
children.note: C++23 closes the classic chained-temporary dangling loophole inside range-based for loops.

children.label: Pre-C++23 __range cliff
children.note: Chaining a member accessor in C++11 through C++20 left the outer temporary dead before iteration.

children.label: C++23 loop-wide lifetime
children.note: P2718R0 extends every temporary in the range-initializer expression until the loop ends.
